claims.finding: Only distinct configured mapped roles conflict; multiple CES entitlement names alone do not trigger rejection. More than one mapped scalar throws MULTIPLE_ROLES. Zero mapped roles throws NO_ROLE_MAPPING. Current config maps only RATAN_ENTITLEMENT_COMMON to FMO_OPS_BOM. Supplied seven-name sample therefore does not itself prove multi-role rejection.
claims.impact: Auth cannot create its legacy/JWT scalar projection for users whose reviewed mappings produce distinct roles. CES-selected conversion ultimately throws unavailable. Shared UI cannot fix login rejection.
claims.remedy: Authoritative scalar compatibility policy, or backend contract that carries structured roles and updates consumers. Do not select first entitlement.

claims.finding: An otherwise structurally valid CES result with zero functional grants throws EMPTY_ACTIONS and cannot pass CES JWT conversion. Whether such users should enter portal is a business policy question; missing grants can represent legitimate no-access, not malformed transport.
claims.impact: If valid no-grant users should retain portal/private flows, login unavailable breaks them. If product denies all no-grant accounts, behavior may be intended.

claims.finding: Resolver returns the first recognized Global/GBS/Onshore entitlement name; other data policy/profile labels resolve to empty. Blank string is accepted by DataEntitlementService; earlier claim that it necessarily fails JWT is unsupported.
claims.impact: The scalar data category is lossy if multiple recognized labels or a new category is valid. It is not the same as an FMO business role and cannot safely fill getUser().role. Deployed downstream interpretation remains unverified.
claims.remedy: Preserve separately defined data-category mapping/precedence and business-role mapping. Existing structured data_filters path remains separate.

claims.finding: Auth chooses EMS3 globally per allowed user and mode; unlike BFF tile provider settings, it has no tile ID. EMS3_PRIMARY_DUAL_READ compares EMS2 but returns EMS3 primary. EMS3_ONLY still uses EMS2 for non-allowlisted users.
claims.impact: A not-yet-migrated tile can use EMS2 UI grants while backend JWT actions/data are already CES for that user. This is a potential assignment/configuration mismatch, not proof every mixed rollout fails.
claims.remedy: For each rollout user ensure CES backend grants cover all usable tiles, or implement backend provider union/routing under agreed policy. Zero UI source changes possible.

claims.finding: Legacy three-argument constructor remains callable but has null FmaaTokenProvider; getEntitlements(userId) then returns empty. Spring bean also obtains optional provider and returns empty if absent. CES base URL and entity mappings additionally required.
claims.impact: Source-compatible consumer can silently lose entitlements unless deployment supplies token provider and CES mapping configuration. No registered deployed caller was found in bounded search.
claims.remedy: Provide shared/injected FMAA token provider and config. Existing getEntitlements(userId) signature can remain. Adding per-caller token API is avoidable if shared wiring supplies provider.

claims.finding: SDK can return multiple entity:role keys, but distinct CES roles cannot alias to one legacy role; config rejects collapsed alias values and duplicate key rejects.
claims.impact: Only consumers requiring many-to-one role aliases encounter this representational gap; no such deployed mapping was verified.
claims.remedy: If authorized policy requires merging, aggregate subject/action grants into one reviewed legacy key in shared SDK. Otherwise use one-to-one mappings.
